A.explanation: 3.0 V is the difference $9.0 - 6.0$, but voltages across series resistors add to give the e.m.f., they are not subtracted.

B.explanation: 6.0 V is only the p.d. across resistor Q from $V = W/Q$, it omits the 9.0 V across P.

C.explanation: 9.0 V is only the p.d. across resistor P from $P = IV$, it omits the 6.0 V across Q.

D.explanation: The sum $9.0 \text{ V} + 6.0 \text{ V} = 15 \text{ V}$ equals the supply e.m.f. for this series circuit with negligible internal resistance.

hints: Notice P and Q are in series in a single loop, so the same 2.0 A flows in both and the supply e.m.f. equals the sum of the two resistor voltages.
For P use the power-current relation $P = IV$ with $18 \text{ W}$ and $2.0 \text{ A}$ to find its p.d.
For Q use the energy-charge relation $V = W/Q$ with $240 \text{ J}$ and $40 \text{ C}$ to find its p.d., then add the two p.d.s.
walkthrough: Identify the circuit: P and Q are connected in series to the supply, so current is the same everywhere and the terminal p.d. equals $V_P + V_Q$.
With negligible internal resistance, terminal p.d. equals e.m.f., so $E = V_P + V_Q$.
Find $V_P$ from $P = IV$. Rearranged, $V_P = P/I = 18/2.0 = 9.0 \text{ V}$.
Find $V_Q$ from energy per unit charge, $V = W/Q$. So $V_Q = 240/40 = 6.0 \text{ V}$.
Add for the series loop: $E = 9.0 + 6.0 = 15 \text{ V}$ with unit check in volts. This is option D.
